paper_claims.claim: The term structure of equity returns is downward-sloping: low-duration stocks earn 1.10% per month more than high-duration stocks (D1-D10 spread).
Classical factor models explain only ~50% of the duration spread: FF3 alpha = 0.84%, FF4 alpha = 0.66%, FF5 alpha = 0.48% per month.
The duration spread is stable across subperiods (1963-1973, 1973-1983, 1983-1993, 1993-2003, 2003-2014).

The negative cross-sectional relationship between duration and returns is concentrated within short-sale constrained stocks (low RIOR); the D1-D10 spread is 1.32% per month for low-RIOR stocks but only 0.15% per month for high-RIOR stocks.

tables.description: Panel A: cross-sectional means and standard deviations of Dur, BM, IOR, PR, ROE, Sales_g, ME, Age (annual averages 1981-2014).
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates that the duration measure (Dechow et al. 2004 implied duration) is correctly constructed from Compustat fundamentals, and that the sample composition (common stocks excl financials/utilities, above 20th size percentile, July 1981-June 2014), 1% winsorization, and the BM, IOR, PR, ROE, Sales_g, ME, Age variable definitions match the paper. Downstream claims C1, C2, C4 all depend on duration being correctly constructed.
tables.paper_quote: This table reports time series averages of annual cross-sectional means and standard deviations for firm characteristics and return predictors in Panel A and contemporaneous correlations of these variables in Panel B. Dur is cash-flow duration; BM is the book-to-market ratio; IOR is the fraction of shares institutions hold; PR is net payout over net income; ROE is return on equity; Sales_g is sales growth; ME is the market capitalization in millions; and Age is the number of years a firm has been on Compustat. ... The sample period is June 1981–June 2014. I only use stocks above the 20th size percentile. (L210)
tables.notes: Panel B correlations are construction-validation only; we replicate the means and std for Panel A. The 1981-2014 sample period follows the paper's "restricted" sample for IOR availability.

tables.description: Monthly mean excess returns, CAPM betas, CAPM alphas, and Sharpe ratios for ten duration-sorted deciles (D1=low, D10=high); D1-D10 spread.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates correct decile-sort portfolio construction (sort by duration at end of June each year 1963-2013, 10 equal-weighted bins, hold 12 months), with the Shumway (1997) delisting treatment and the sample filters (NYSE/AMEX/NASDAQ common stocks, excl financials/utilities). This is the table that tests the headline claim C1.
tables.paper_quote: At the end of June each year $t$ from 1963 to 2013, I sort stocks into ten deciles based on duration for the fiscal year ending in calendar year $t - 1$ . I rebalance portfolios on an annual basis and weight returns within portfolio equally. ... Panel A reports monthly mean excess returns, time series factor loadings ( $\beta$ ), and pricing errors ( $\alpha$ ) for the CAPM for ten portfolios sorted on duration (Dur) with OLS standard errors in parentheses in Panel A. (L339, L376)
tables.notes: Tables 2 Panel A only; we skip Panel C (value-weighted) and Panel D (no delisting) for budget — they are robustness.

tables.description: FF3, FF4, and FF5 alphas for the ten duration-sorted deciles and the D1-D10 spread.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates that the factor models are correctly constructed (FF3 = Mkt-RF + SMB + HML; FF4 = FF3 + Mom; FF5 = FF3 + RMW + CMA), the time-series regressions are correctly estimated, and that the duration spread is not absorbed by classical risk factors. Tests claim C2.
tables.paper_quote: This table reports pricing errors ( $\alpha$ ) for the Fama and French three-factor model ( $\alpha_{F\&F3}$ ), the three-factor model augmented with momentum ( $\alpha_{F\&F4}$ ), and the Fama and French five-factor model ( $\alpha_{F\&F5}$ ) for ten portfolios sorted on duration (Dur) with OLS standard errors in parentheses. (L595-599)
tables.notes: Decile-level FF3 alphas (10 cells) + spread alphas for FF3, FF4, FF5 (13 cells). Decile-level FF4/FF5 alphas are omitted for budget — the spread carries the claim.

tables.description: Monthly mean excess returns for the ten duration-sorted deciles in five 10-year subsamples (1963-1973, 1973-1983, 1983-1993, 1993-2003, 2003-2014).
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates that the duration spread is temporally stable and not driven by a single regime. Tests claim C3. Exercises the same sort/portfolio mechanics as Table 2 but variable window slices — confirms the methodology is correct even if the sample boundary differs.
tables.paper_quote: This table reports monthly mean excess returns with OLS standard errors in parentheses for different subsamples. I sort all common stocks listed on NYSE, AMEX, and NASDAQ at the end of June each year $t$ from 1963 to 2013 into deciles based on duration for all firms with fiscal years ending in year $t-1$ . (L1126)
tables.notes: Replicate the D1-D10 spread in each of 5 subperiods (5 cells) plus selected D1/D10 means for visual spectrum check (6 cells).

tables.description: Monthly mean excess returns for 25 portfolios sorted on duration (quintiles) and residual institutional ownership (RIOR) (quintiles), 1981-2013.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates that the duration spread is concentrated among short-sale constrained stocks (low RIOR), and that the spread decreases in RIOR. Tests the central mispricing claim C4. Exercises the RIOR construction (Eq. 7) and the double-sort methodology.
tables.paper_quote: Table 10 reports monthly mean excess returns for the 25 portfolios. We see a pronounced downward-sloping term structure of equity returns for stocks with low residual institutional ownership, which are potentially the most short-sale constrained. Low-duration stocks earn an excess return of 1.02% per month. The return decreases monotonically in duration. High-duration stocks earn an excess return of –0.30% per month. The spread in excess returns for the two extreme-duration portfolios is 1.32% per month and highly statistically significant. (L2010-2011)
tables.notes: Partial replication: 17 cells (rows of Dur x RIOR cells for 5 RIOR bins x 2 extreme Dur quintiles + the D1-D5 spread). The full 25-cell grid is encoded as 17 selected cells; the spreadsheet-level structure is documented but not cell-by-cell.
